title: Foundations for Life — Building Good Habits God's Way
description: Test your understanding of personal responsibility, time management, hygiene, organization, manners, and goal-setting from a Biblical stewardship perspective.

questions.question: According to Galatians 6:5, what does God expect from each person?
options: That others will carry your burdens for you
That each person should carry their own load
That only adults need to be responsible
That responsibility is optional for believers
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:5 teaches that each person should carry their own load, meaning God calls everyone to take personal responsibility for their actions and duties.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 5:15-16 teach about how Christians should use their time?
options: Time does not matter as long as you pray
Fill every moment with work and never rest
Be wise and make the most of every opportunity
Only use time for spiritual activities
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:15-16 calls us to live wisely and make the most of every opportunity. This means being intentional and purposeful with our time, not wasting it.

questions.question: Why does the Bible call our bodies 'temples of the Holy Spirit' (1 Corinthians 6:19-20)?
options: Because our bodies are made of stone like a temple
Because God's Spirit lives in believers, so our bodies should be honored and cared for
Because we should worship our bodies
Because temples are old and outdated
questions.explanation: God's Holy Spirit lives in believers, making our bodies sacred dwelling places. This means we should care for our bodies through good hygiene and healthy habits as an act of worship.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:40, how should things be done?
options: As quickly as possible
However you feel like doing them
In a fitting and orderly way
Only when you are told to
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:40 teaches that everything should be done in a fitting and orderly way. God is a God of order, and organizing our lives reflects His character.

questions.question: What is the foundation of good manners according to Luke 6:31?
options: Following a long list of rules
Doing to others as you would have them do to you
Always agreeing with everyone
Being quiet and staying out of the way
questions.explanation: The Golden Rule — treating others as you want to be treated — is the foundation of all good manners. Courtesy flows naturally from a heart that values others.

questions.question: What does SMART stand for in goal setting?
options: Simple, Meaningful, Active, Reasonable, Temporary
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
Strong, Motivated, Ambitious, Reliable, Tough
Spiritual, Moral, Attentive, Respectful, Thankful
questions.explanation: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. This framework helps turn vague wishes into clear, actionable plans.

questions.question: What is procrastination, and what does the Bible say about it?
options: Working too hard; the Bible encourages rest
Putting off tasks you should do now; the Bible warns against laziness
Doing tasks ahead of time; the Bible says this is prideful
Asking others for help; the Bible says this shows weakness
questions.explanation: Procrastination means putting off what you should do now. The Bible warns against laziness and uses the ant as an example of diligence (Proverbs 6:6-8).

questions.question: According to Proverbs 16:3, what should we do with our plans and goals?
options: Keep them secret from everyone
Only set goals that are easy to achieve
Commit them to the Lord and trust Him to establish them
Abandon all planning and just see what happens
questions.explanation: Proverbs 16:3 tells us to commit our plans to the Lord and trust Him to establish them. Goal setting is important, but we should always invite God into the process and trust His guidance.
